title: Master Services Agreement

issues.quote: 1. For each engagement, the parties shall sign a statement of work in the form of Schedule 1 (each, a "Statement of Work") describing the services for that engagement (the "Services"), the Deliverables, the fees, and the schedule.
issues.why: Numbered schedule; house rule 6 gives schedules letters and exhibits numbers.
issues.fix: in the form of Exhibit 1 (a form is an exhibit; see the classification issue)

issues.anchor: SCHEDULE 1 – FORM OF STATEMENT OF WORK
issues.quote: SCHEDULE 1 – FORM OF STATEMENT OF WORK
issues.why: The statement-of-work form is a stand-alone document, so it belongs in an exhibit, not a schedule (house rule 6).
issues.fix: Retitle it "EXHIBIT 1 – FORM OF STATEMENT OF WORK" and refer to "Exhibit 1" in the body.

issues.anchor: Statement of Work shall be effective
issues.quote: 2. Each Statement of Work shall be effective when both parties have signed it.
issues.why: No duty; "shall be effective" is language of policy written as obligation.
issues.fix: Each Statement of Work is effective when both parties have signed it.

issues.quote: 2. Provider shall use best efforts to meet each delivery date in a Statement of Work.
issues.why: Mixed efforts standards: "best efforts" here, "reasonable efforts" for Customer in the section titled "Customer Responsibilities." Mixing invites the argument that 2 different standards apply (MSCD ch. 8).
issues.fix: Provider shall use reasonable efforts to meet each delivery date in a Statement of Work.

issues.quote: 4. Provider's subcontractors shall comply with Customer's site-safety rules while at any Customer terminal.
issues.why: Provider's subcontractors don't sign this agreement, so "shall" can't bind them.
issues.fix: Provider shall cause its subcontractors to comply with Customer's site-safety rules while at any Customer terminal.

issues.quote: 5. Provider shall comply with the Customer's information-security policies that Customer gives Provider in writing.
issues.why: House rule 11: no article before the defined party name "Customer" (used without "the" everywhere else).
issues.fix: Provider shall comply with Customer's information-security policies that Customer gives Provider in writing.

issues.anchor: within 30 days of the invoice date
issues.quote: 2. Customer shall pay each invoice within 30 days of the invoice date.
issues.why: "Within 30 days of" doesn't say before or after the invoice date.
issues.fix: Customer shall pay each invoice no later than 30 days after the invoice date.

issues.quote: 3. Customer shall reimburse Provider for travel expenses incurred by Provider in performing the Services, if Customer approved the travel in writing in advance.
issues.why: Recastable reduced passive (no article before the noun).
issues.fix: Customer shall reimburse Provider for travel expenses that Provider incurs in performing the Services, if ...

issues.quote: 4. Customer may share the reports prepared by Provider with Customer's lenders, auditors, and insurers.
issues.fix: Customer may share the reports that Provider prepares with Customer's lenders, auditors, and insurers.

issues.quote: 3. Provider grants Customer a nonexclusive, perpetual, royalty-free license to use that software as part of the Work Product.
issues.why: "Work Product" is never defined; it appears once, apparently meaning the Deliverables (2 forms for 1 thing).
issues.fix: Provider grants Customer a nonexclusive, perpetual, royalty-free license to use that software as part of the Deliverables.

issues.quote: 2. Provider's liability is limited to $250,000 for claims arising out of this agreement.
issues.why: Unclear whether the $250,000 cap applies to each claim or to all claims in the aggregate.
issues.fix: Provider's total liability for all claims arising out of this agreement is limited to $250,000 in the aggregate (or: $250,000 for each claim).

issues.anchor: arising out of or relating to
issues.quote: Each party shall bring any claim arising out of or relating to this agreement only in the state or federal courts in King County, Washington.
issues.why: "Arising out of or relating to" is broader and vaguer than needed (MSCD 13.41-13.54).
issues.fix: Each party shall bring any claim arising out of this agreement only in the state or federal courts in King County, Washington.

traps.anchor: Customer is not required to purchase
traps.quote: 3. Customer is not required to purchase any minimum volume of Services.

2. The Receiving Party shall use the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information only for this agreement and shall not disclose it to anyone other than the Receiving Party's employees and contractors who need to know it for this agreement.
traps.why_correct: Role labels ("the Receiving Party", "the Disclosing Party") keep "the" (house rule 11).

traps.quote: 4. Customer shall pay Provider a one-time onboarding fee of $7,500 when the parties sign the 1st Statement of Work.
traps.why_correct: "One-time" is part of a word, not a count; "the 1st Statement of Work" correctly uses a digit.
Section I. correctly follows H.; the house scheme uses every letter, I included.

notes: The file already holds 3 Word comments by "Dana Whitlock" (on the liability cap in the section titled "Limitation of Liability", on the insurance text in "Insurance", and on the Schedule 1 heading). They are business points, not drafting issues: a review should keep them and not count them as findings. Issue 4 (mixed efforts standards) is anchored at "best efforts"; a finding anchored at Customer's "shall use reasonable efforts to make" that names the inconsistency should count as a match for issue 4, and Customer's "reasonable efforts" wording is itself correct. Issues 1 and 2 share 1 fix (Exhibit 1). Defined terms inside the statement-of-work form ("the MSA") are correct. Font Aptos 12, left-aligned, typed house enumeration (A. to J., subsections 1.).
